hints.content:
$f$ is increasing in an interval where as $x$ increases, $f(x)$ also increases.

Visually, this is where the graph is going upwards as we go from left to right.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by one. The graph of y equals f of x is a continuous curve. From left to right, it passes through the point negative five, one-half and it decreases through the x-intercept negative four and three-quarters, zero and the point negative four, negative one and one quarter. It decreases until the local minimum at negative three, negative two. Then it increases through the point negative two, negative one, the x-intercept negative one and one-half, zero, and the point negative one, one. It increases until the local maximum at zero, two. Then it decrease through the point one, one, the x-intercept one and one-half, zero and the point two, negative one. It decreases until the local minimum at three, negative two. Then it increase through the point four, negative one and one quarter and the x-intercept four and three-quarters, zero. All values are estimated. The function is highlighted from x equals negative three to x equals zero and after x equals three.

hints.content:
Now we can check each option:

Interval | Is $f$ increasing on the interval?
:-: | :-:
$-3<x<-2$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
$-1.5<x<0$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
$3.5<x<4.5$ |  $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
